title: MZ Does anyone know of a good game with zero plugins?

posts.author: AlvieRomy
posts.body: I'm having lots of fun learning RPGMaker, I'd like my first project to not use any plugins and I'd like to play a game which is the same so I can get an idea of what's possible (Honestly I'm not even familiar with the genre of 2D rpgs). Thank you if you know of anything.

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
I guess it depends on whether you allow use of scripts or not, since that alone will give you lots of stuff to work with. It's probably best to just do the built-in tutorial to give you an idea. But with clever use of Show Picture and (a lot of) patience I suspect you can go a long way.
There was a game jam in the past it seems.

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome to the forum!
While I get your goal and I appreciate the sentiment since it is one that I believe I share, I'd actually recommend NOT trying to avoid ALL plugins since that would be unnecessarily limiting. MZ actually comes with some very useful default plugins. For instance, I lean heavily on the TextPicture and ButtonPicture plugins that come with MZ, because of the type of game I am developing.
I'm a firm believer in learning what you can do with just MZ itself and using Javascript with the Script event command instead of just defaulting to a plugin at every turn. I think it helps you build a much more solid foundation for continued learning.
And I can't count the number of times I've seen someone posting a question on the forum for where to find a plugin to do something and one of the first answers they get is that you don't even need a plugin for what you are trying to do. Because their default is that there must be a plugin to do everything instead of learning what MZ can do with just the standard Event Commands and some scripting.
But, I think you might be better off trying to use as little plugins as possible and to avoid the mistake of just downloading a bunch of plugins because everyone else does that.
In my current Sudoku project, I'm only using the default MZ plugins and a couple of very small, custom plugins that do very specific things. Like a simple key mapping plugin, a simple skip title screen plugin, a simple change save file name plugin, etc. All of those simple custom plugins are small pieces of javascript code that folks on the forum helped me with.
Other than the game jam that restricted the use of plugins, I'm not sure how you would really know if a released game did or didn't use any plugins unless it was stated by the developer.
Anyway, again, I would advocate that you keep your options open to using default plugins that come with MZ and very simple plugins that serve a specific purpose if you get to a point where there isn't any other option. Some things you might want to do and experiment with in a game project just can't be done without a plugin.
That is very different from using larger scale plugins that do all sorts of things, many of which you might not even need.
Of course, there's nothing wrong with trying to make a game without ANY plugins to experiment with how that works out. If it is in the spirit of learning how to use MZ, then it is probably worth it.
Anyway, good luck on your project and don't turn out like Zombie, who has been using MZ for over 3 years now and doesn't have ANY experience with using all of the readily available plugins that do lots of very interesting things. It's on my list of things to learn.
